claims.sentence: <jats:title>SUMMARY</jats:title><jats:p><jats:bold>Background</jats:bold> : Aspirin is widely used as an anti‐thrombotic drug; however, it has been suggested that enteric‐coated formulations of aspirin may be less bioavailable and less effective as anti‐thrombotic agents.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Aim</jats:bold> : To assess the effect of a formulation of enteric‐coated, low‐dose (81 mg) aspirin on serum generated thromboxane B<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> and platelet aggregation in healthy subjects.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:bold>Methods</jats:bold> : Twenty‐four subjects participated in a double‐blind, randomized, placebo‐controlled, parallel‐group, multiple‐dose study.
